description: Fires on moves with significant eval loss. Severity tier + side-specific framing + a concrete WHY clause when the extractor produced one. Suppression block keeps the rule from saying anything when we have no concrete fact AND the loss isn't blunder-tier.

fact_glossary.best_move_san: Engine's preferred move (when different from played)
fact_glossary.severity_phrase: Authored phrase ('is a mistake' / 'is a serious mistake' / 'is a major blunder') — picked from severity_phrases by severity_tiers
fact_glossary.why_clause: Optional appended sentence — Python pre-renders the why_clauses_user/opp entry that matches, sets facts['why_clause'] before evaluating select_variant
fact_glossary.moving_piece_type: Type of the piece that just moved
fact_glossary.opp_reply_san: Opponent's strongest reply (PV[0] after the played move)
fact_glossary.captured_piece_type: Piece type the opponent's reply would capture
fact_glossary.user_best_reply_san: User's strongest reply after an opp blunder
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_kind: Climax of pv_after_best — 'mate' | 'piece_capture' | 'material' | absent. Set by best_move_tactic_detector by walking the engine's recommended line and finding the tactical payoff (mate / wins a piece / wins pawns).
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_target_piece: When missed_tactic_kind = piece_capture: the piece type won (e.g. 'queen', 'rook').
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_target_square: When missed_tactic_kind = piece_capture: the square on which the piece was won.
fact_glossary.missed_tactic_ply: When missed_tactic_kind = mate: number of plies in the PV to checkmate.
fact_glossary.shape_pattern_id: Geometric pattern fired on the pre-move board (e.g. 'king_pawn_lifted', 'h7_attack', 'pin'). Set by V5 service before render via shape_layer.select_shape_for_position.
fact_glossary.shape_pattern_target_square: Square the shape pattern is centered on (e.g. 'f7' for a king_pawn_lifted on Black's f7).
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_attack_square: Square that the engine's best move would have opened up for attack via clearance (Légal's / Fried Liver family). Set by V5 service when simulate_clearance_for_attack(best_move) fires on the pre-move position.
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_attacker_piece: Lowercase piece name (queen / rook / bishop) of the slider whose line would have been opened by best_move. Used by the missed_clearance_attack why-clause to name the piece in coach voice instead of internal 'slider' jargon.
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_piece: Lowercase piece name (queen / rook / bishop) of the slider that would have given check after the best move's clearance — Légal's-Mate family. 2-move plan: best_move opens the line, the named slider plays a check on the next move. v56 (2026-05-22) — fix to v53's overcorrection that dropped 2-move detection entirely; see memory/feedback_fix_framing_not_detection.
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_destination: Square the slider moves to after the best move's clearance to deliver the check (e.g. 'h5' for Qh5+).
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_follow_up_sa: Hand-built SAN of the slider's check move (e.g. 'Qh5+'). Computed by detect_clearance_then_check via a null-move push to flip turn before board.san().
fact_glossary.missed_clearance_then_check_king_square: Square of the king being chased (e.g. 'e8'). Names the target plainly in the caption.
fact_glossary.attack_with_tempo_piece: Lowercase piece-name (queen/rook/bishop/knight/pawn) the engine's best move attacks, where opp's PV[1] retreats THAT piece. v57 (2026-05-22) — captures the 'with tempo' tactical pattern from Mohit's approved captions #1 (Qe2/d4 hits bishop on c5) and #2 (e4/Nh4 hits bishop on f5). Excludes king (checks are a different family — queen-fork pattern).
fact_glossary.attack_with_tempo_square: Square where the attacked piece sat (e.g. 'c5'). Used by the why_user_missed_attack_with_tempo template to name the target plainly.
fact_glossary.attack_with_tempo_follow_up_san: SAN of the engine's PV[2] move — what white plays AFTER opp retreats the attacked piece. Often a capture (Bxf4, Bxb7) that defines the tactical payoff. Optional; when absent the template just names the tempo attack without the follow-up.
fact_glossary.queen_fork_sub_kind: 'capture_with_check' (queen captured a piece on its destination AND gives check) or 'fork' (queen moves to a square attacking king + another undefended opp piece). v61 (2026-05-22) — Mohit approvals #5 (Qb3+), #16 (Qh4+), #19 (Qxb4+).
fact_glossary.queen_fork_secondary_piece: Lowercase piece name of the captured/forked target (the non-king target).
fact_glossary.queen_fork_king_square: Square of the opp king under check.
fact_glossary.endgame_loose_pawn_sub_kind: 'direct_capture' (best move IS the capture, e.g. Kxh3) or 'attack' (best move attacks the pawn, e.g. Rf3 → next Rxh3). v62 (2026-05-22) — Mohit approvals #13, #15.
fact_glossary.endgame_loose_pawn_moving_piece: Lowercase piece-name doing the grabbing (king / rook / bishop / knight / queen).
fact_glossary.endgame_loose_pawn_square: Square of the loose (undefended) opp pawn.
fact_glossary.missed_capture_target_piece: v100+ (Mohit fb_ee2ec3abeffd 2026-05-27). Lowercase piece-name (pawn / knight / bishop / rook / queen) sitting on best_move.to_square when the engine's best_move is a CAPTURE that didn't trigger missed_tactic_kind=piece_capture (i.e. small material gain like a pawn). Pairs with missed_capture_target_square. Fills the gap where why_user_defensive_pawn_push previously claimed 'passive pawn move' when the real teaching was 'you missed a capture' (game_692ab776c5b1 m7 a6 — engine wanted Bxc5 winning the pawn).
fact_glossary.best_move_is_sacrifice: True when the engine's best move is a capture whose ATTACKER is worth more than the captured target AND the destination is defended after the capture (= the attacker is lost to recapture). Drives why_user_missed_capture_sacrifice variants — stops 'wins the pawn' framing on knight sacrifices (Parth fb_6f2a5ba1f626 / Nxh3+ pattern).
fact_glossary.best_move_sac_attacker_piece: Piece name of the sacrificed piece (the moving piece in the sacrifice). Used in sac variant text.
fact_glossary.best_move_sac_near_king: True when the sacrificed-on square is within 2 squares of the enemy king AND the captured piece is a pawn — king-shred sacrifice pattern.
fact_glossary.missed_capture_target_square: Destination square of the engine's missed capture (e.g. 'c5').
fact_glossary.un_developing_piece: v63 — Mohit approval #4 (Bf1 retreated to home). Lowercase piece type the user retreated to its starting home square.
fact_glossary.un_developing_from: Square where the developed piece was sitting before the retreat (e.g. 'e2').
fact_glossary.un_developing_home: Starting home square the piece retreated to (e.g. 'f1').
fact_glossary.defensive_pawn_user_san: v63 — Mohit approval #7 (b3 instead of Bd3). The passive pawn move the user played.
fact_glossary.defensive_pawn_best_dev_san: The piece-developing move (or castling) the engine wanted instead.
fact_glossary.knight_outpost_destination: v63 — Mohit approval #11 (Ne4). Central square the engine wants to outpost the knight on. Defended by own piece; not attackable by enemy pawns.
fact_glossary.knight_outpost_defender_piece: Own piece defending the outpost (e.g. 'bishop' for Bg2 defending Ne4).
fact_glossary.stop_opp_pawn_blocking_san: v63 — Mohit approval #14 (a5 stopping a4-a5). The engine's blocking pawn move.
fact_glossary.stop_opp_pawn_opp_square: The opp pawn being blocked from advancing.
fact_glossary.active_defense_defended_piece: v64 — Mohit approval #12 (Qe7 defends b4 + attacks e5). Own piece being saved.
fact_glossary.active_defense_defended_square: Square of the threatened own piece.
fact_glossary.active_defense_attacked_piece: Opp piece newly under attack from the engine's move.
fact_glossary.active_defense_attacked_square: Square of the counter-attacked opp piece.
fact_glossary.same_piece_better_extra_piece: v64 — Mohit approval #8 (Qe4/Qf5). Lowercase piece name of an opp piece the engine's destination attacks but user's destination does not.
fact_glossary.same_piece_better_shared_piece: Lowercase piece name of an opp piece BOTH destinations attack (the shared target). Optional.
fact_glossary.same_piece_better_shared_square: Square of the shared target. Optional.
fact_glossary.discovered_vac_moved_piece: v64 — Mohit approval #6 (Qa5/Nxd3+). Lowercase piece name that gave check on the destination square.
fact_glossary.discovered_vac_slider_piece: Lowercase piece name of the own slider whose attack line just opened.
fact_glossary.discovered_vac_exposed_piece: Lowercase piece name of the opp piece newly exposed to the slider.
fact_glossary.discovered_vac_exposed_square: Square of the newly-exposed opp piece.
fact_glossary.knight_on_rim_square: v65 — Mohit approval #9 (Na6/e5). Square (a-file or h-file) the user moved their knight to in the opening.
fact_glossary.pawn_kicks_piece_type: v65 — Mohit approval #10 (Qd7/c4 — c4 kicks Bb3). Lowercase piece-name being kicked by engine's pawn push.
fact_glossary.pawn_kicks_piece_square: Square of the piece being kicked.
fact_glossary.why_clause_em_dash: v66 — Mohit 2026-05-22 voice match. Set true by V5 service when one of the new best-move-focused detectors fires (queen_fork, attack_with_tempo, clearance_then_check, endgame_loose_pawn, active_defense, same_piece_better_square, discovered_vacating_check, knight_outpost, stop_opp_pawn, pawn_kicks_piece, missed_clearance_attack, missed_piece, missed_material, knight_on_rim, un_developing, defensive_pawn_push, trap_context_name). When true, R12_blunder uses the em-dash parent variant ('Y was better — reason') matching Mohit's approved voice, instead of the default 'Y was better. Reason.' two-sentence form.
fact_glossary.trap_context_name: v69 — Mohit 2026-05-22 ('trap and openings ship next whatever applies'). Display name of a known opening trap whose setup was reached but whose punishment (trap_line[0]) the user MISSED — i.e. the user is the trap's setter/punisher in scanner terminology, and the engine's best_move equals trap_line[0]. Set by V5 service from services.trap_scanner output, with the trailing ' Punishment' / ' Trap' suffix stripped so it flows in the caption template ('Damiano Defense Punishment' → 'Damiano Defense'). Highest-priority why-clause — when set, fires why_user_missed_trap_punishment which names the trap as the textbook refutation.
fact_glossary.trap_context_full_name: v69 — original trap name before suffix-stripping (e.g. 'Damiano Defense Punishment'). Kept for downstream consumers that want the canonical library name.
fact_glossary.trap_context_first_punishment_san: v69 — trap_line[0], the engine-recommended punishment move that matches best_move_san when trap_context_name is set. Available to other variants that may want to name the move explicitly.
fact_glossary.trap_context_description: v69 — hand-authored description from data/traps.json (e.g. 'Black plays 2...f6 (the Damiano), inviting a knight sacrifice...'). Not currently used by the default template (descriptions vary in flow and aren't designed to drop cleanly into caption prose), but available for future variants or LLM polish.
fact_glossary.opening_name: v69 — Mohit 2026-05-22 + [[opening-name-only-at-critical-lessons]]. Detected opening from detect_opening_from_pgn (e.g. 'Italian Game', 'Damiano Defense'). Set ONLY when a trap also fires — naming the opening at every move would be noise per the memory rule. Reserved for genuinely critical lesson moments.
fact_glossary.position_was_already_losing: true when the user's eval has been losing (<= -150cp from user POV) for the last 3+ user moves before this one. Tells the caption to frame the move as 'damage control' rather than 'source of the loss' — the real problem is earlier in the game.
fact_glossary.losing_since_move: Earliest move number in the contiguous losing run. Used by the with-known variant to point the user back at where the position started going wrong.
fact_glossary.piece_type: Piece-type generic placeholder used by hanging-piece why-clauses
fact_glossary.square: Square placeholder used by hanging-piece why-clauses
fact_glossary.mover_is_user: true if the mover is the user
fact_glossary.opp_reply_attacks_played_piece: true when opp's PV[0] directly attacks the just-moved piece
fact_glossary.is_exchange_losing: true when the move itself landed on a losing-exchange square
fact_glossary.pieces_now_undefended_present: true when at least one own piece is now undefended (set by Python from the pieces_now_undefended list)
fact_glossary.opp_pieces_now_undefended_present: true when at least one opp piece is now undefended after their blunder
fact_glossary.opp_played_landed_unsafe: true when opp's move stranded their own piece
fact_glossary.best_move_san_differs: true when best_move_san is present AND != played_san
fact_glossary.opp_reply_san_is_check: true when opp's PV[0] ends with '+' or '#'
fact_glossary.user_best_reply_san_is_forcing: true when user_best_reply_san ends with '+' or '#'
fact_glossary.curriculum_deviation_clause: Hand-authored wrong_feedback from opening_curriculum.json — the tree's teaching for the deviation the user just played. Set by V5 service when get_opening_guidance reports is_in_book=True with expected_move ≠ played_san. Priority above generic blocked_pawn / board_state detectors but below concrete-about-played-move clauses (hanging, capture, check, exchange_losing) so a tactical 1-move blunder still wins over book-theory teaching.
fact_glossary.curriculum_expected_move: The book-theory move the tree expected the user to play (set alongside curriculum_deviation_clause).
fact_glossary.curriculum_opening_name: The matched opening's position_name from the curriculum.
fact_glossary.user_is_winning: true when user_eval_after >= +200cp from user POV. Triggers user_winning_position variant for cp_loss < 250 with no why_clause — reframes 'X is a mistake' as 'X is fine, you're still winning' (per Mohit 2026-05-21: when up by a queen, no positional move should be labeled 'a mistake' — it's misleading coaching).
fact_glossary.user_is_losing: true when user_eval_after <= -200cp. Triggers user_losing_position — reframes as context ('you were already losing') instead of blame.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_file: File letter ('a'..'h') of a user pawn whose advance was blocked by the played piece move. Set by principle_blocked_pawn detector when the engine's best move was a pawn move to square X and the user played a non-pawn piece to X. Fires the why_user_blocks_own_pawn variant — names the opening principle the user just violated (don't block your own central pawn support).
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_square: The target square (e.g. 'c3') the user's pawn would have moved to.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_would_support: The first central-pawn square (e.g. 'd4') the user's pawn would have supported diagonally. Only set when the pawn would have supported a real central pawn — gives the why-clause its specific teaching value.
fact_glossary.blocked_pawn_would_prepare: Central square (e.g. 'd4') the blocked pawn push would have PREPARED — a user pawn on the file behind it is one push away. Parth fb_6e38c6a6f53e: distinguishes 'c3 prepares the d4 break' (d-pawn still on d3) from 'c3 supports an existing d4 pawn'. Drives why_user_blocks_pawn_prepares.
fact_glossary.board_state_clause: Pre-rendered 1-3 sentence string describing the post-move board state from user's POV (Mohit 2026-05-21). Composed in Python by board_state_describer: pick top 3 facts (with diversity across categories), render each from a bs_* template, join with '. '. Fires as why-clause when nothing more specific did — universal fallback that stays in coach voice rather than engine-speak.
fact_glossary.bs_piece: Piece type placeholder for individual bs_* templates (e.g. 'knight')
fact_glossary.bs_square: Square placeholder for individual bs_* templates (e.g. 'e5')
fact_glossary.bs_user_developed: Count of user minor pieces developed (off home squares) — used by bs_development_gap
fact_glossary.bs_opp_developed: Count of opp minor pieces developed — used by bs_development_gap
fact_glossary.bs_back_rank_count: Count of user minor pieces still on starting back rank — used by bs_pieces_on_back_rank
fact_glossary.bs_king_square: User's king square — used by bs_king_* templates
fact_glossary.bs_missing_shield: Count of missing shield-pawn squares in front of king — used by bs_king_shield_broken
fact_glossary.bs_attacker_count: Count of distinct opp pieces attacking user's king zone — used by bs_king_attackers
fact_glossary.bs_user_central: Count of user attacks on central squares (e4/d4/e5/d5) — used by bs_central_control_gap
fact_glossary.bs_opp_central: Count of opp attacks on central squares — used by bs_central_control_gap
fact_glossary.bs_file_letter: File letter ('a'..'h') of an open file controlled by opp major — used by bs_open_file_owned_by_opp
fact_glossary.bs_opp_major_piece: Piece type ('rook' or 'queen') controlling the open file — used by bs_open_file_owned_by_opp
fact_glossary.bs_queen_square: User's queen square when she's the only active piece — used by bs_queen_alone_active
fact_glossary.bs_passive_count: Count of user non-pawn pieces still in own-side ranks — used by bs_passive_pieces_count

_trigger_note: v76 (2026-05-23): lowered cp_loss threshold 100→30 so opp INACCURACIES (cp_loss 30-99) can also fire R12 — combined with the v76 opp-narration wiring (user_best_reply_san), this surfaces 'Opponent's X is a mistake. You can play Y to punish it.' on previously-silent opp inaccuracies like Parth's m4 Be6 (cp=88) and m9 Be7 (cp=72). User-side low-cp moves stay silent via suppression (mover_is_user:true + why_clause:absent + cp_loss<250) — only opp moves with a why_clause set make it through.
_severity_tiers_note: v79.3 (2026-05-25): Mohit caught cp_loss=76 opp move with severity='opp_inaccuracy' being rendered as 'is a mistake.' Old severity_tiers only had three steps and dumped everything below 250 into the 'mistake' bucket — including small inaccuracies (30-99) that V5's severity classifier separately marks as 'opp_inaccuracy' / 'inaccuracy'. Added a fourth tier so the caption phrase tracks V5's severity classification: blunder (>=400) / serious mistake (>=250) / mistake (>=100) / inaccuracy (30-99).
_user_engine_meta_dropped_note: v94 (2026-05-25): why_user_missed_material ('it wins material in the resulting line') + why_user_reply ('Opponent's strongest reply: X') removed entirely. Mohit 2026-05-25 on Tier B Q2: 'stop pretending every move deserves a concrete caption. silence is NOT always worse. silence is better than fake explanation. V5's biggest strength is supposed to be: only speak when grounded. Don't betray that principle because you fear empty UI.' These two why-clauses were the last engine-speak fallbacks — they fired when no concrete detector had a reason to give, and surfaced engine moves without explaining WHY. Now: when no concrete why-clause fires on a user mistake, the why_clause stays empty and the variant selector falls to user_with_best ('X is a mistake. Y was better.') without engine-meta apologies. Result: ~30-40% more user-side mistake-tier moves render without a why-clause, but the ones that DO render are grounded.
_user_engine_speak_gate_note: v77.1 (2026-05-23): the two engine-speak fallbacks (why_user_missed_material 'it wins material in the resulting line' / why_user_reply 'Opponent's strongest reply: X') now require cp_loss >= 100. Without this gate, the v76 R12 trigger lowering (100 -> 30) made these fire on user INACCURACIES (cp_loss 30-99) that V5's severity classifier separately marks as 'good' — producing captions like 'Nf6 is a mistake. Nc6 was better. Opponent's strongest reply: O-O.' on moves V5 considered fine. Now: user inaccuracies below 100 cp_loss are either silenced (when no concrete detector fired) or surface a concrete why-clause (when one did). The opp-side why-clauses are unaffected — opp moves still get full opp-narration treatment at the 30 threshold.

variants.user_winning_position: {played_san} is fine — you're still winning. {best_move_san} would have kept the pressure on.
variants.user_losing_position: {played_san} doesn't change much — you were already losing. {best_move_san} would have made the loss slower.
variants.why_user_missed_trap_punishment: it's the textbook refutation in the {trap_context_name}.
variants.why_user_missed_mate: it would have led to mate in {missed_tactic_moves_to_mate} {missed_tactic_mate_word}.
variants.why_user_missed_clearance_attack: it clears the line for your {missed_clearance_attacker_piece} to attack {missed_clearance_attack_square}.
variants.why_user_missed_clearance_then_check: it opens the line, and your {missed_clearance_then_check_piece} can then play {missed_clearance_then_check_follow_up_san} to chase the king on {missed_clearance_then_check_king_square}.
variants.why_user_missed_attack_with_tempo_full: it hits the {attack_with_tempo_piece} on {attack_with_tempo_square} with tempo. Your follow-up: {attack_with_tempo_follow_up_san}.
variants.why_user_missed_attack_with_tempo: it hits the {attack_with_tempo_piece} on {attack_with_tempo_square} with tempo.
variants.why_user_missed_queen_capture_with_check: it captures the {queen_fork_secondary_piece} on {queen_fork_secondary_square} with check, winning material.
variants.why_user_missed_queen_fork: it forks the king on {queen_fork_king_square} and the undefended {queen_fork_secondary_piece} on {queen_fork_secondary_square}.
variants.why_user_missed_endgame_pawn_grab: it grabs the undefended pawn on {endgame_loose_pawn_square}. In the endgame, hunt undefended pawns with your active pieces.
variants.why_user_missed_endgame_pawn_attack: it attacks the undefended pawn on {endgame_loose_pawn_square}, and your {endgame_loose_pawn_moving_piece} can grab it next move. In the endgame, hunt undefended pawns with your active pieces.
variants.why_user_missed_capture: it captures the {missed_capture_target_piece} on {missed_capture_target_square}. Before every move, scan for free captures — material won is leverage you keep.
variants.why_user_missed_capture_sacrifice_king: it sacrifices your {best_move_sac_attacker_piece} to break open the pawn shield in front of their king. The attack that follows is worth more than the {missed_capture_target_piece} given up.
variants.why_user_missed_capture_sacrifice: it sacrifices your {best_move_sac_attacker_piece} for compensation. The engine sees an attack or tactic worth more than the {missed_capture_target_piece}.
variants.why_user_un_developing: Don't retreat a developed piece without a reason — keep your pieces active.
variants.why_user_defensive_pawn_push: In the opening, don't waste tempo on a passive pawn move — develop a piece toward the center instead.
variants.why_user_missed_knight_outpost: it puts your knight on a strong outpost: defended by your {knight_outpost_defender_piece} on {knight_outpost_defender_square}, safe from any enemy pawn.
variants.why_user_missed_stop_opp_pawn: it blocks the opponent's pawn before it advances further. When your opponent threatens a pawn push, blocking it is often more important than developing.
variants.why_user_missed_active_defense: it defends your {active_defense_defended_piece} on {active_defense_defended_square} AND attacks the undefended {active_defense_attacked_piece} on {active_defense_attacked_square}. Active defense — defending while creating your own threat — beats passive defense.
variants.why_user_missed_same_piece_better_square: it also hits the {same_piece_better_extra_piece} on {same_piece_better_extra_square}. The same piece on a square that attacks more targets is the stronger move.
variants.why_user_missed_discovered_vacating_chec: it grabs material with check AND clears the way for your {discovered_vac_slider_piece} to take the {discovered_vac_exposed_piece} on {discovered_vac_exposed_square}.
variants.why_user_knight_on_rim: Knights on the rim are weak — in the opening, knights belong near the center, not the edge.
variants.why_user_missed_pawn_kicks_piece: it attacks the {pawn_kicks_piece_type} on {pawn_kicks_piece_square}, forcing it to move. Pawn pushes that attack enemy pieces gain tempo — the opponent has to react.
variants.why_user_position_already_losing_since_k: You were already in trouble since move {losing_since_move}. {best_move_san} only slows it — the problem started earlier.
variants.why_user_position_already_losing: You were already in trouble before this move. {best_move_san} only slows the loss.
variants.why_user_blocks_pawn_supports: {played_san} blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn — {best_move_san} would have supported your {blocked_pawn_would_support} pawn.
variants.why_user_blocks_pawn_prepares: {played_san} blocks your {blocked_pawn_file}-pawn — the pawn push to {blocked_pawn_square} was preparing your {blocked_pawn_would_prepare} break, the central plan in this structure.
variants.why_user_attacks_played: After {opp_reply_san}, your {moving_piece_type} on {target_square} is under attack.
variants.bs_isolated_attacker: Your {bs_piece} on {bs_square} is alone in opponent territory with no defender.
variants.bs_development_gap: Opponent has developed {bs_opp_developed} pieces; you've developed {bs_user_developed} {bs_user_developed_word}.
variants.bs_pieces_on_back_rank: You still have {bs_back_rank_count} minor pieces on the back rank.
variants.bs_king_shield_broken: Your king on {bs_king_square} has lost {bs_missing_shield} of its pawn shelter.
variants.bs_king_attackers: {bs_attacker_count} opponent pieces are aimed at your king on {bs_king_square}.
variants.bs_central_control_gap: Opponent attacks the center {bs_opp_central} {bs_opp_central_word}; you attack it {bs_user_central} {bs_user_central_word}.
variants.bs_open_file_owned_by_opp: The {bs_file_letter}-file is open and opponent's {bs_opp_major_piece} controls it.
variants.bs_queen_alone_active: Your queen on {bs_queen_square} is the only piece doing anything.
variants.bs_connected_rooks_only_opp: Opponent's rooks are connected; yours aren't yet.
variants.bs_passive_pieces_count: {bs_passive_count} of your pieces are still on your side of the board.
variants.why_opp_hanging: Their {piece_type} on {square} is now undefended — take it.
variants.why_opp_user_queen_capture_with_check: Play {user_best_reply_san} — your queen captures the {opp_user_reply_queen_fork_secondary_piece} on {opp_user_reply_queen_fork_secondary_square} with check.
variants.why_opp_user_queen_fork: Play {user_best_reply_san} — your queen forks their king and the {opp_user_reply_queen_fork_secondary_piece} on {opp_user_reply_queen_fork_secondary_square}.
variants.why_opp_user_clearance_then_check: Play {user_best_reply_san} — opens the line so your {opp_user_reply_clearance_piece} can play {opp_user_reply_clearance_follow_up_san} to chase their king.
variants.why_opp_user_clearance_attack: Play {user_best_reply_san} — clears the line so your {opp_user_reply_clearance_attacker_piece} attacks {opp_user_reply_clearance_attack_square}.
variants.why_opp_user_attack_with_tempo: Play {user_best_reply_san} — hits their {opp_user_reply_attack_piece} on {opp_user_reply_attack_square} with tempo.
variants.why_opp_user_kicks_piece: Play {user_best_reply_san} — your pawn kicks their {opp_user_reply_kicks_piece_type} on {opp_user_reply_kicks_piece_square}.
variants.why_opp_user_kicks_piece_with_check: Play {user_best_reply_san} — your pawn forks their king and {opp_user_reply_kicks_piece_type} on {opp_user_reply_kicks_piece_square}.
variants.why_opp_user_endgame_pawn_grab: Play {user_best_reply_san} — grabs their undefended pawn on {opp_user_reply_endgame_pawn_square}.
variants.why_opp_user_endgame_pawn_attack: Play {user_best_reply_san} — attacks their undefended pawn on {opp_user_reply_endgame_pawn_square}.
variants.why_opp_wing_pawn_push: {opp_played_wing_pawn_san} is a wing-pawn push in the opening — doesn't develop a piece or fight for the center. Play {user_best_reply_san}.
variants.why_opp_knight_on_rim: {opp_played_knight_on_rim_san} parks the knight on the rim ({opp_played_knight_on_rim_square}) — knights attack fewer squares from the edge. Play {user_best_reply_san}.
variants.why_opp_queen_early: {opp_played_queen_early_san} brings the queen out before their minor pieces — you can chase it and gain tempo. Play {user_best_reply_san}.
variants.why_opp_un_developed: {opp_played_un_developed_san} retreats the {opp_played_un_developed_piece} back home — wastes a tempo, undoes their earlier development. Play {user_best_reply_san}.
